newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-BOCA COACH TO FINE SHIRT-SWAPPERS $30,000.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOCA COACH TO FINE SHIRT-SWAPPERS $30,000.

text.p: Desperate to restore his team's pride and get them winning again, Boca Juniors troubled coach Carlos Bilardo has said he will fine players $30,000 for swapping their shirts with opponents.

"I told players that a Boca shirt is worth $30,000, like a car and that from now on I'm in charge of the locker room wardrobe," Bilardo said, according to Argentine newspapers Wednesday. "They're not going to swap shirts any more."

Bilardo was enraged last Sunday when Boca crashed to another defeat, going down 1-0 against Independiente. Midfielder Cristian Dollberg was reprimanded by the coach when he went to swap his shirt with an opponent after the match.
Bilardo immediately excused temperamental star Diego Maradona from the new rules: "The only one who's allowed to make a swap, because he's world-famous, is Maradona. The rest have to keep them on."
The overweight Maradona, who last week struggled through his first training session for over two months, is once again speculating about retirement and is unlikely to play anyway.

Bilardo, who coached the Argentine national team to World Cup finals in 1986 and 1990, set a record for the local league at the beginning of the season by reportedly spending $20 million overhauling the team.
But the team from Buenos Aires' port area is currently ninth on the table.
